target_customer: Independent artists, musicians, indie producers and video production companies who sell video content and live shows directly to fans
problem: Creators needed one place to publish video, monetize it through pay per view and subscriptions, and reach fans on connected TV apps without building distribution themselves.
business_model: Creator platform taking a share of pay per view, micro-subscription and merch revenue (as described by YC; the revenue split is not stated)
product_category: Creator video publishing and monetization platform

founders.name: Ashutosh Nayak
prior_employers: Large US media conglomerates (per YC page, specific names not listed)
education: MBA, MIT Sloan School of Management
founders.background_notes: YC page says over a decade building products and technology for US media companies. The March 2021 press release says the company was founded by former executives of ViacomCBS, NBC, Amazon and Audible.

founders.name: Vaibhav Kharat
education: Master's in Industrial Engineering, University of Cincinnati
MBA, MIT Sloan School of Management

technical_complexity.rationale: Video hosting, payments and apps for Apple TV, Roku and Fire TV are standard engineering but multi-platform app delivery and 4K streaming were a heavy load for a team of three listed on the YC page.

defensibility.rationale: The offering of pay per view, subscriptions and merch drops for creators was a bundle of features other video platforms could copy; no data, network or contract moat is described in the sources.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source documents what incumbents did in response; the company's wind-down cause is not public.

market_need_then: The pitch compared itself to Substack for video creators during the 2020 to 2021 pandemic period, when live and paid online concerts grew. No quantified demand evidence was found in the sources opened.

branding.domain_note: Used the gigs.live domain (a .live name rather than .com); the host no longer resolves from this environment.

identity.voice_and_tone: Pitch language borrowed the Substack analogy for creators

branding.community_and_virality: The March 2021 launch release says fans could form their own tribes around artists; no independent coverage of the brand was found.

brand_strength.rationale: Searches returned only the YC page and aggregators, and other companies with similar names (Giggs, GigSalad) crowd results, which points to little brand awareness.

outcome_analysis: YC lists Gigs Live as inactive but no article, post-mortem or company notice explaining the cause was found, so the cause of the wind-down is not public. The only dated history is the March 2021 launch release for a hybrid physical and virtual concert platform, and no funding was found, which leaves the result unexplained rather than attributable to a factor.
notes: Website gigs.live did not resolve (fetch failed with a DNS error), so it is treated as dead or blocked. No funding found in outcome or funding searches; funding aggregators were paywalled. No competitor with a source dated near the Winter 2021 batch was found, so the list is empty. Exit type is unknown because the shutdown is not documented anywhere I could open. One aggregator describes the company as a live events career platform, which conflicts with the creator video description and is treated as a name confusion.
